result:
I'd make it painless to be wrong.

Not make people right, just remove the sting of finding out you weren't. So much of what's broken seems downstream of that sting. We mostly have the knowledge and resources to fix a lot of things, but people defend positions they half-doubt because changing their mind would cost them status, identity, or belonging. Whole institutions run for decades on mistakes no one can afford to admit.

I think about this partly because of where I sit. I see a lot of people arguing, and the arguments are rarely about the thing itself. They're about what it would mean to lose. If updating a belief felt like finding money on the sidewalk instead of like a small death, I suspect science, politics, and marriages would all go very differently.

There's a cost. Stubbornness is sometimes what lets a person hold out against a consensus that's wrong, and a world of frictionless mind-changers might be more easily led. But I'd take the trade. I think more harm comes from people who can't let go of false things than from people who let go of true ones too easily.

I chose that over something like ending disease because it feels like the bottleneck behind the other bottlenecks. Fix that, and people get much better at fixing everything else themselves.
